cards.title: Introduction to Form Validation in Vue
cards.content: Form validation is a crucial part of any web application. In Vue.js, you can build custom validation logic or leverage powerful ecosystem libraries like VeeValidate or Vuelidate to handle complex rules, error messages, and asynchronous validation efficiently.

options.text: Vuex is primarily used for form validation.
VeeValidate and Vuelidate are popular dedicated validation libraries for Vue.
Vue.js requires jQuery for validating inputs.

cards.title: Native v-model Modifiers
cards.content:
Before reaching for third-party libraries, Vue provides built-in modifiers for v-model that help sanitize and validate input types:

  • .number: Casts user input string to a valid number.
  • .trim: Automatically trims whitespace from user input.
  • .lazy: Syncs input after the change event instead of input.
<input v-model.number.trim="age" type="number" />

content.text: To automatically remove leading and trailing whitespace from a text input in Vue, use the v-model [blank] modifier.

cards.title: Setting up VeeValidate
cards.content:
VeeValidate integrates seamlessly with Composition API and Yup for schema validation. Here is a basic setup:

import { useForm, useField } from 'vee-validate';
import * as yup from 'yup';

const schema = yup.object({
  email: yup.string().required().email(),
});

const { handleSubmit } = useForm({ validationSchema: schema });
const { value: email, errorMessage } = useField('email');

cards.title: Asynchronous Validation
cards.content:
Sometimes you need to check if a username or email already exists in the backend database. Yup and VeeValidate support async rules easily:

const schema = yup.object({
  username: yup.string().required().test(
    'is-taken',
    'Username is already taken',
    async (value) => {
      const response = await checkUserAPI(value);
      return response.available;
    }
  )
});

steps: User enters data into form fields
v-model updates reactive state and modifiers sanitize input
VeeValidate triggers schema validation against Yup rules
Errors are displayed reactively in the template if invalid
handleSubmit callback is executed if all validations pass

cards.title: Form Validation Best Practices
cards.content:
Keep these practices in mind when designing forms in Vue:

  • Validate on blur or submit to avoid annoying users while they are still typing.
  • Provide clear, accessible error messages right next to the offending input.
  • Always perform backend validation as well; client-side validation is for UX, not security.

options.text: Client-side validation is completely sufficient for application security.
Client-side validation improves UX, but server-side validation is mandatory for security.
Vue.js automatically secures all database writes against malicious input.
